stories.title: 81,000 warning letters sent to crypto holders in HMRC tax crackdown
stories.summary: HMRC sent more than 81,000 letters, emails and texts to cryptocurrency investors suspected of underpaying Capital Gains Tax in the 2025-26 financial year — the largest such enforcement action to date. The data-driven crackdown comes after new powers requiring crypto exchanges to report user data to HMRC.

stories.title: UK borrows more than expected in July as Healey prepares for first Budget
stories.summary: UK government borrowing came in higher than forecast in July, putting pressure on Chancellor John Healey ahead of his inaugural Budget in October. Healey confirmed the government remains 'committed to meeting its fiscal rules'.

stories.title: Customs checks to move closer to border
stories.summary: HMRC has announced plans to relocate customs checks closer to the UK border as part of ongoing trade facilitation reforms, aiming to reduce friction at ports and streamline import processing.

stories.title: Asylum appeals target launched for faster removals
stories.summary: The Home Office has introduced a new 24-week target for asylum appeal decisions, meaning individuals with no right to remain in the UK will be deported faster. The policy is part of broader efforts to reduce the asylum backlog.

stories.title: Prison overcrowding presents PM Burnham with first major test
stories.summary: The prison overcrowding crisis is proving to be PM Andy Burnham's first significant challenge, with the early release scheme creating difficult choices — including questions over which prisoners should be excluded. The Home Secretary is under pressure to resolve the situation quickly.

stories.title: New guide for asylum seekers on UK behaviours and expectations published
stories.summary: The Home Office published updated guidance aimed at asylum seekers arriving in the UK, setting out expected behaviours and legal obligations during the asylum process.

stories.title: Joint statement: Israel closing investigation into strikes on World Central Kitchen convoy
stories.summary: The UK, Australia and Canada issued a joint statement responding to Israel's decision to close its investigation into the deadly April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen aid convoy, expressing serious concern about the outcome and calling for accountability.

stories.title: PM Burnham to provide Ukraine with long-range weapons support
stories.summary: The Burnham government is set to announce a further package of military and diplomatic support for Ukraine, including commitments on long-range weapons systems, as the conflict continues.

stories.title: UK crackdown on Russia with tough new sanctions
stories.summary: The FCDO announced further sanctions against Russian individuals and entities as part of the UK's ongoing response to the conflict in Ukraine and Russian economic activities.

stories.title: Millions to receive benefit payments early ahead of August bank holiday
stories.summary: DWP confirmed that all major benefit payments due on Monday 31 August 2026 (August bank holiday) will be brought forward to Friday 28 August. This covers Universal Credit, State Pension, PIP, Carer's Allowance, DLA and many more, helping families plan ahead of the new school year.

stories.title: Reform UK's plan to cut £50bn from welfare bill scrutinised
stories.summary: BBC Verify has examined Reform UK's proposals to cut more than £50bn per year from welfare spending, with experts questioning the feasibility of the figures. The analysis comes as the government debates the future of disability benefits.

stories.title: DWP completes full migration of legacy benefits to Universal Credit
stories.summary: The Department for Work and Pensions has confirmed the completion of its migration of all legacy benefit claimants to Universal Credit, with only a tiny number of exceptional cases remaining on the old system.

stories.title: New drought support package announced for farmers
stories.summary: DEFRA announced a new drought support package for farmers as parts of England face prolonged dry conditions. The announcement was made during a ministerial visit to a farm in Cornwall and includes financial assistance and guidance on water management.

stories.title: Government to clean up UK's three worst illegal waste dumps
stories.summary: PM Burnham announced government action to tackle the UK's three worst illegal waste dumps in Kent, Surrey and West Yorkshire, containing an estimated 22,000 tonnes of waste. The move is part of broader environmental enforcement efforts.

stories.title: Coordinated drought response intensifies
stories.summary: DEFRA's coordinated drought response is being intensified, with the department working with water companies, farmers and local authorities as dry conditions persist across parts of England.

stories.title: UK armed forces step up monitoring of increased Russian activity in UK waters
stories.summary: Royal Navy warships and helicopters spent 21 days on operations monitoring Russian naval activity in UK waters and the North Atlantic throughout July. The MoD confirmed the increased activity reflects a heightened security environment.

stories.title: Delays to defence plan undermine UK credibility, MPs say
stories.summary: A cross-party group of MPs has warned that delays to publishing the UK's defence plan are undermining the country's credibility with allies. The criticism comes as armed forces minister Al Carns insists spending needs to 'go faster'.

stories.title: Defence Secretary visits Rosyth Shipyard to champion Scotland's defence role
stories.summary: Defence Secretary John Healey visited Babcock's Rosyth shipyard and service family accommodation in Edinburgh, declaring that 'Scotland is powering Britain's future defence' and highlighting investment in Scottish shipbuilding.

stories.title: £13 million boost to drive next-gen satellite communications for trains and farmers
stories.summary: BIST announced a £13 million funding package to improve satellite connectivity, including better WiFi on remote train routes and cutting-edge communications technology for British farmers. The investment supports the UK's wider space and connectivity strategy.

stories.title: G7 deal agreed to ramp up AI adoption among SMEs
stories.summary: UK Tech Minister Ian Murray returned from the G7 Summit with a new international agreement to accelerate AI adoption among small and medium-sized businesses. The deal also includes stronger tech ties between the UK and Canada.

stories.title: AI for Science Strategy sets out UK's plan for frontier technologies
stories.summary: BIST published its AI for Science Strategy, targeting five priority frontier industries — advanced materials, fusion energy, medical research, engineering biology, and quantum technology — as part of the UK's modern industrial strategy.

stories.title: Salmonella outbreak: 207 cases and one death linked to imported eggs
stories.summary: The UK Health Security Agency declared a national outbreak of Salmonella Enteritidis with 207 confirmed cases and one death, linked to imported eggs. Health officials are investigating the supply chain and advising the public on food safety.

stories.title: NHS keeps its cool as temperatures and demand soar
stories.summary: NHS England reported that health services managed elevated demand during the summer heatwave, with staff responding effectively to increased attendances at emergency departments. The NHS activated heat health protocols to protect vulnerable patients.

stories.title: 100,000 people cured of deadly Hepatitis C on the NHS in ten years
stories.summary: NHS England celebrated a major milestone: 100,000 people have now received curative treatment for Hepatitis C since the NHS began its elimination programme a decade ago. The UK is on track to eliminate the virus as a public health threat.

stories.title: MPs accuse Royal Mail of 'lying' and prioritising parcels over letters
stories.summary: A cross-party group of MPs accused Royal Mail bosses of 'lying' about prioritising parcel deliveries over letters, leading to widespread postal delays. Royal Mail appeared before a parliamentary select committee to answer questions, denying the allegations and promising to publish a delivery improvement plan.

stories.title: Royal Mail given two weeks to respond to allegations of letter de-prioritisation
stories.summary: Royal Mail has been formally given two weeks to respond to allegations that it is systematically prioritising parcel deliveries over letters, resulting in significant delays affecting millions of customers — including missed hospital appointments and delayed financial documents.

stories.title: Second-class letter delivery moves to alternate-day schedule
stories.summary: From 28 July 2026, Royal Mail moved to an alternate-day delivery schedule for second-class letters, meaning they are now delivered on Monday, Wednesday and Friday rather than every weekday — a significant change to the universal service.
